pr_title: Change ConfigurationBinder to avoid reading properties unnecessarily.
pr_body:
Previously, ConfigurationBinder would eagerly read properties it
encountered and initialize/bind objects for them even when those
reads/initializations could lead to thrown exceptions or unnecessary
work. Now, we defer work until we determine that it will actually
contribute to the final binding result.

Fix #52905
Fix #65710

issue_context.title: Configuration binder failed when getter of read only property throw exception
issue_context.body:
### Description

# The problem

When I try to add a read only property, what based on my configuration, the Binding of configuration will throw the following exception.

```
System.Reflection.TargetInvocationException: Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation.
 ---> System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'source')
   at System.Linq.ThrowHelper.ThrowArgumentNullException(ExceptionArgument argument)
   at System.Linq.Enumerable.Where[TSource](IEnumerable`1 source, Func`2 predicate)
   at BindPropertyExceptionSample.Configuration.get_FilteredConfigValues() in C:\Source\Github\BindPropertyExceptionSample\BindPropertyExceptionSample\Configuration.cs:line 5
   --- End of inner exception stack trace ---
   at System.RuntimeMethodHandle.InvokeMethod(Object target, Span`1& arguments, Signature sig, Boolean constructor, Boolean wrapExceptions)
   at System.Reflection.RuntimeMethodInfo.Invoke(Object obj, BindingFlags invokeAttr, Binder binder, Object[] parameters, CultureInfo culture)
   at System.Reflection.RuntimePropertyInfo.GetValue(Object obj, BindingFlags invokeAttr, Binder binder, Object[] index, CultureInfo culture)
   at System.Reflection.PropertyInfo.GetValue(Object obj)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationBinder.BindProperty(PropertyInfo property, Object instance, IConfiguration config, BinderOptions options)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationBinder.BindNonScalar(IConfiguration configuration, Object instance, BinderOptions options)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationBinder.BindInstance(Type type, Object instance, IConfiguration config, BinderOptions options)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationBinder.Bind(IConfiguration configuration, Object instance, Action`1 configureOptions)
   at Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.ConfigurationBinder.Bind(IConfiguration configuration, Object instance)
   at Program.<Main>$(String[] args) in C:\Source\Github\BindPropertyExceptionSample\BindPropertyExceptionSample\Program.cs:line 12
```

# Sample
Configuration.cs
```csharp
public class Configuration
{
    public IEnumerable<int> FilteredConfigValues => ConfigValues.Where(p => p > 10);
    public IEnumerable<int> ConfigValues { get; set; } = null!;
}
```
appsettings.json:
```json
{
    "Logging": {
        "LogLevel": {
            "Default": "Debug",
            "System": "Information",
            "Microsoft": "Information"
        }
    },
    "TestConfig": {
        "ConfigValues": [ 1, 10, 100, 1000 ]
    }
}
```
Program.cs
```csharp
using BindPropertyExceptionSample;

using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;

var config = new ConfigurationBuilder()
    .AddJsonFile("appsettings.json")
    .Build();

var testConfig = new Configuration();
config.GetSection("TestConfig").Bind(testConfig); // The exeption will be thrown here.

Console.WriteLine($"Filtered config values: {string.Join(", ", testConfig.FilteredConfigValues)}");
```

# Reason

The `ConfigurationBinder.BindProperty` is reading the value of the property before it decide is there setter of property.
At this line: [`object? propertyValue = property.GetValue(instance);`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7da602644b7088233a13d5c7202d0aabcd0e29f6/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/src/ConfigurationBinder.cs#L236)

### Reproduction Steps

You can find a repository with a sample code of the issue [here](https://github.com/lenraven/BindPropertyExceptionSample).

### Expected behavior

Skip the read only properties during the binding.

### Actual behavior

An exception was thrown when I call the Bind of configuration.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

Target framework: NET 6.0
SDK: 6.0.101
Operating system: Windows 10
Architecture x64


### Other information

_No response_

Thanks for the report. Just noticed that this NRE stacktrace is pointing to the where clause below in the user code itself, during the `Bind` call:

```c#
public class Configuration
{
    public IEnumerable<int> FilteredConfigValues => ConfigValues.Where(p => p > 10);
    public IEnumerable<int> ConfigValues { get; set; } = null!;
}
```

```
System.Reflection.TargetInvocationException: Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation.
 ---> System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'source')
   at System.Linq.ThrowHelper.ThrowArgumentNullException(ExceptionArgument argument)
   at System.Linq.Enumerable.Where[TSource](IEnumerable`1 source, Func`2 predicate)
   at BindPropertyExceptionSample.Configuration.get_FilteredConfigValues() in C:\Source\Github\BindPropertyExceptionSample\BindPropertyExceptionSample\Configuration.cs:line 5
   --- End of inner exception stack trace ---
```

This looks like a very corner case bug.

Let's make sure to add a test case for the regression scenario that was reported in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/63479

>Fact [](http://example.com/codeflow?start=9&length=4)

do we have a test case like the case mentioned in [https://github.com/lenraven/BindPropertyExceptionSample/tree/master/BindPropertyExceptionSample](https://github.com/lenraven/BindPropertyExceptionSample/tree/master/BindPropertyExceptionSample)?

I mean the order of the properties can make difference too.

Prior to this change, we'd assign `List<T>`s to settable `IEnumerable<T>`, `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` and `IReadOnlyList<T>` properties. Now these will be arrays. I think this is okay, just pointing it out.

@halter73 good callout; I should have left a comment about this. I made the change just to reduce some otherwise-duplicative code. As you say, I think it should be ok. Hopefully noone is assuming they can cast one of the read-only interfaces to a specific concrete implementation.
Calling Activator.CreateInstance on a List can't ever return null, right?
It is unlikely to return null for List<T>. I am seeing we didn't check for Dictionary<,> too in the next method.
That's what I thought; just wanted to highlight the change.
